title: Endpoint
body:
A specific URL, paired with a specific [[HTTP Verb]], that a server has a handler registered for — `GET /api/reviews/123`. In the restaurant analogy it's one item on the menu. Endpoints are defined and hosted entirely on the server: the client can request any URL it likes, but if no handler matches, the server's router answers 404 (unknown path) or 405 (known path, wrong method).

Note that path and endpoint aren't the same thing. `/api/reviews/:id` is a *route pattern* with a parameter, and the concrete `/api/reviews/123` is what the client actually calls; [[Express]] route handlers in Web Development for CS work exactly this way. See [[REST]] for how endpoints get organised.
